answers.rationale: Maya repeatedly prioritizes the closest, strongest-reviewed business hotel over a modest saving or included breakfast when the location reduces daily friction. C is also the least expensive, closest, and highest rated option. It properly treats breakfast as a verification item rather than assuming that review mentions mean the selected refundable rate includes it.

For family trips, Maya consistently favors nonstop travel and three assigned adjacent seats over modest savings, open seating, or a better carrier-specific preference. A preserves all three seats together on nonstop flights; B adds a connection, C has unassigned Southwest seating, and D separates the family across nearby rows.

D retains the low-friction convention-center access Maya values for early workdays without a car, while also giving her a confirmed desk for the prep call and included breakfast. The covered one-block route is operationally close to the attached hotel, and keeping the official hotel as fallback preserves the stronger-location alternative if the selected rate changes.

Maya's repeated rule is nonstop when sensible, otherwise one short connection—not multiple stops or hours of waiting. A has one reasonable 1-hour-20-minute connection, arrives with ample time before the 4 p.m. event, and avoids B and D's very long layovers and C's two-connection itinerary.
